correctness.rationale: The symmetric-design distance shells give singular-sector eigenvalues −2^p ± √q(3^p−1) and a one-dimensional part-contrast eigenvalue, with the stated multiplicities. At q=2 the nonincidence contrast is negative at the singular root; for q≥3 the contrast crosses before 1/q while the singular eigenvalue is still negative. In RESULT.md line 91 the contrast alone need not rule out every larger exponent (it can turn negative again); the interval-property argument explicitly allowed there is sufficient. Strictness below the endpoint follows from the Bernstein integral for a smaller power of a CND kernel: the Gaussian matrices tend to identity as the scale grows, so the integral is strictly negative on every nonzero contrast. The distinct-point Gaussian conclusion concerns positivity for all positive scales, not necessity at an individual scale. Centered Gram rank and Taylor expansion verify the dimensions and constants. Inspected RESULT.md, VERIFICATION.md and checker.py; the recorded finite checks do not certify generality, and the script was not executed.
